bridge: Full witness hypergraphs -> hypergraph certificate complexity / invariant compression
novelty_signal: Promote. The benchmarked package now exports validated full-witness hypergraphs for baseline gaps 13, 17, 19, 20, 21 and late gaps 21, 25, 28, 30 with multiplicity mismatch count 0, so the last serious H1 rescue is finally testable on all-witness data rather than lossy first-witness logs.
validation_plan: Use the existing full-hypergraph exports to measure description length per skipped value, interval-level motif growth, factor-usage concentration, and simple structural proxies such as edge density and cover-size concentration; require these summaries to stabilize across gaps 21, 25, 28, 30 and remain more compressible than size-matched surrogate product sets.
risk: This can still collapse into generic local product coverage if motif counts and description length grow roughly linearly with gap size.

bridge: Mex-coupled frontier -> size-matched surrogate product-set ablation
novelty_signal: Promote. The falsifier and novelty audit identify Ford-style divisor/product coverage as the main overlap risk, and the variant benchmark shows that the negative conclusions survive nearby rule perturbations. A direct surrogate-control comparison is now the cleanest test of whether any surviving invariant is genuinely T-specific.
validation_plan: Construct null product sets that preserve row/column marginal sizes, gap-adjacent factor histograms, and simple axis offsets while breaking mex coupling; compare singleton share, balanced-factor share, axis-marker frequency, hypergraph motif counts, and compressed signature length against the true process.
risk: If the surrogates match the true process on those summaries, the positive-mechanism program is effectively dead and only the negative-result dossier survives.

bridge: Prime-separator witness logs -> practical numbers / dense divisors interval-extension
novelty_signal: Hold. This remains a strong control bridge because practical-number style extension chains are the right standard for compact local coverage, but the current corpus shows the tiny-factor language decaying and balanced witnesses rising, so the bridge looks more useful as a falsifier than as a proof scaffold.
validation_plan: For each late record gap, sort usable border factors by size and test whether a uniformly bounded prefix forces most of the skipped interval via interval-extension inequalities; compare the required prefix length against the true hypergraph summaries and the surrogate controls.
risk: The required factor prefix may keep growing with the gap, turning the bridge into another way of certifying failure rather than proving boundedness.

bridge: Full witness corpus -> numerical semigroups / numerical monoids factorization invariants
novelty_signal: Hold. Exact witness pairs are too heterogeneous, but higher-level factorization-graph invariants could still stabilize on the newly validated full hypergraphs. This is the best remaining rescue route if raw witness labels are already dead.
validation_plan: Compute invariant vectors per skipped value and per interval, including pair-count spectrum, smallest-factor bucket, largest-factor bucket, balancedness bucket, axis participation, and simple factor-graph connectivity summaries; test cluster stability from the 30k corpus to the 1M corpus and across the row_immediate and column_immediate variants.
risk: The invariants may simply rename the existing heterogeneity without beating simpler witness statistics or surrogate controls.

bridge: Raw witness stream -> substitution / automaton / low-complexity symbolic law
novelty_signal: Retire. The verifier already concludes that the raw witness language does not compress into a compact T-specific certificate, late record gaps remain singleton-heavy, and the only stable motif is the one-point axis-1 marker.
validation_plan: No active budget. Revisit only if bucketed hypergraph invariants first produce a stable finite alphabet that materially outperforms shuffled or surrogate baselines.
risk: Keeping this active now would amount to symbolic relabeling of a witness story that already failed.

bridge: Prime split / prime-support fixed point -> gap control
novelty_signal: Retire. H2 was explicitly killed by the verifier: composite-only record gaps occur at 17, 20, 21, 28, and 30, and the prime-support observables change too smoothly to explain record-gap jumps.
validation_plan: No active budget unless a genuinely new support observable predicts record-gap behavior better than the direct witness logs.
risk: High OEIS overlap and no demonstrated explanatory gain.

bridge: Frontier repair by mex -> parking processes / jamming
novelty_signal: Retire as an active mechanism bridge. The probe results say this analogy is acceptable phenomenology for vacancy clusters but does not separate T-specific certificates from generic local coverage.
validation_plan: None for the current concept cycle; only revive if a later empirical study needs a descriptive model of gap-length distributions rather than a proof-oriented mechanism.
risk: It encourages descriptive analogy without clearing the overlap bar or producing a witness-level invariant.
